content.text:
I added a dark theme to `index.html`, `style.css` and `app.js`. It follows the OS setting by default, and a new button in the header switches between System, Light and Dark. I haven't opened it in a browser yet. I also tried a JavaScript syntax check, but that command needed your approval and didn't run.

**How it works:**
- **Colors (`style.css`):** All the hard-coded colors are now shared color values that the dark theme overrides. Dark mode turns on when you pick Dark, or when you're on System and your OS is set to dark. Because CSS handles the System case, switching your OS theme updates the page right away, even with JavaScript off. The dark colors are written out twice in the file, so if you change one copy, change the other to match.
- **Built-in controls:** Date pickers, scrollbars and similar browser controls also switch to their dark versions.
- **No flash on load (`index.html`):** A small script at the top of the page applies the saved choice before anything is drawn, so a saved Dark choice doesn't briefly show the light page first.
- **The button (`app.js`):** It shows an icon and the current mode, and each click moves to the next one: System → Light → Dark. Light and Dark are saved in the browser's local storage; picking System clears the saved value. If storage isn't available (e.g. some private-browsing modes), the button still works but the choice isn't kept for the next visit.

**Two light-mode changes to note:**
- Text inputs now have their own background, border and rounded corners so they look right in dark mode. That makes them look a little different in light mode too.
- The header is now laid out as a row, so the title sits on the left and the button on the right.
